title: Gold, silver prices in Indian markets crash to nearly a year’s low - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
On Wednesday, gold was down over 2 per cent at $3,772 an ounce at 1300 hrs IST, while silver was quoted at $45.90 an ounce. The precious metals have plunged to their lowest in over a year in the global market as the dollar strengthened on hopes of the US Fed raising interest rates faster than expected. | Photo Credit: istock.com

Gold and silver prices in India dropped to their lowest level in a year on Wednesday, in line with the global trend amid a strengthening dollar. Globally, precious metals prices are at a 14-month low

Data from the Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association showed that the price of yellow metal for pure gold (.999 fineness) opened at ₹1,31,505 per 10 g compared with the closing price of ₹1,34,201 on Tuesday. Silver opened at ₹1,64,506 a kg against ₹1,69,171 on Tuesday evening.

Gold’s rate is lower than the opening price of ₹1,33,151 on January 1. The last time prices were above today’s rate was on December 12, 2025, when the yellow metal opened at ₹1,30,569.

Gold prices have dropped by about ₹10,000 per 10 g since the beginning of this month as the global market has been heading southward.

In the case of silver, the opening price on January 1 was ₹2,27,900 a kg. The last time the white precious metal’s prices hovered lower than today was on November 28, 2025, at ₹1,64,286.

On Wednesday, gold was down over 2 per cent at $3,772 an ounce at 1300 hrs IST, while silver was quoted at $45.90 an ounce. The precious metals have plunged to their lowest in over a year in the global market as the dollar strengthened on hopes of the US Fed raising interest rates faster than expected.

In the futures market, gold for December delivery was quoted at $3,769, while silver December delivery ruled at $45.78 an ounce. On MCX, gold December contracts were ₹1,31,060 per 10 g, and silver December contracts were ₹1,63,533 a kg at 1315 hours.

Gold and silver peaked at $5,608 an ounce and $121.74 an ounce on January 29 this year. Since then, they have declined by over 30 per cent and 62 per cent, respectively.

Renisha Chainani, chief research officer at Augmont, said investors are now waiting for the minutes of the Federal Reserve’s meeting for clues on where policy is headed, after the crash due to the dollar and US Fed rate cut hopes.

Darshan Desai, CEO, Aspect Bullion & Refinery, said from the bullion industry’s perspective, consumer buying remains cautious, with people closely tracking daily price movements before making purchase decisions.

“While the recent correction may encourage some buying, particularly among jewellers and wedding-related buyers, consumers are largely opting for selective and staggered purchases rather than bulk buying,” he said.

Manav Modi, commodities analyst, Motilal Oswal Financial services Ltd, said escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia could offer some support, as regional media reports suggest Iran’s IRGC launched missiles and drones at warships near Qeshm Island.

Desai said going ahead, global economic cues, currency movements and geopolitical developments will influence prices. “We expect volatility to continue, with physical demand remaining measured as consumers look for favourable buying opportunities,” he said.
